stories.title: Texans Work for Free on Farms That Aren't Theirs to Send Others' Kids to College
stories.label: people
stories.summary: In Texas, residents volunteer their time to farm land that isn't theirs, and the money it raises goes to college scholarships for kids they don't know. The tradition is now 15 years old. In that time it has paid out $3 million in scholarships. It's a simple idea that has quietly helped a lot of young people get to college.
stories.why_good: A community has turned free labor into $3 million of real college help for young people over 15 years.

stories.title: Family Is Thankful Their Baby, Given Weeks to Live on Christmas Eve, Now Brain Cancer-Free
stories.label: health
stories.summary: An infant girl was told she had only weeks to live from an aggressive brain cancer. Her case landed at a hospital that had just finished a careful study of her exact type of cancer. That study had been run at St. Jude Children's Hospital, one of 15 institutions involved. With that fresh knowledge behind her care, she has made a full recovery and is now cancer-free, just in time for her family to give thanks.
stories.why_good: A child with a grim prognosis is now cancer-free, thanks to research that had just been completed and put to use.
